title: Sunset Playbook for Legacy 'Signal' Endpoints with Client Fallback Strategy
creator: Marcus Chen
description:
Why: The legacy 'signal' endpoints (signal.generate, signal.stream) were an early transport layer for internal experiments. They now add maintenance surface area, increase client compatibility complexity, and block unified inference optimizations (batching, KV caching, kernel selection). This ticket defines a risk-minimized, observable deprecation path that preserves client availability via a built-in fallback adapter and clear migration guidance for SDKs and integrators.

What: A playbook covering timeline, adapter runtime, telemetry gates, migration CLI & SDK changes, customer communications, canary strategy, and rollback criteria. The playbook must enable teams to safely retire the endpoints without manual intervention by clients where feasible, while giving enterprise customers migration windows and opt-out controls.

Non-goals: We are not re-implementing new features in the legacy transport or extending long-term support beyond the stated sunset windows. No changes to billing model are included in this ticket.
scope_changes: Initial scope: design playbook + adapter + SDK patches + docs + canary rollout. Scope change allowed: if the adapter introduces >5% performance regression on critical paths, split rollout into smaller QOs and add dedicated perf work (separate ticket). Any customer-specific adapter work is out-of-scope and will be triaged as professional services requests.
migration_steps: 1) Publish migration RFC and migration checklist for integrators: mapping of signal.generate -> unified.generate, mapping streaming frames to chunked deltas.
2) Implement compatibility adapter on gateway level: request translation + header shim + response envelope compatibility. Default: shadow mode for 2 weeks.
3) Release SDK patch (v1.12.0) that warns on use of 'signal' endpoints and offers an automatic adapter-opt-in flag.
4) Enable adaptive routing experiments to route 5% traffic through unified endpoints while keeping adapter in-path for verification.
5) Open early-access migration for top 10 customers with support engineers assigned for 4-week collaboration windows.
6) Execute phased traffic ramp: shadow -> 5% -> 25% -> 60% -> 100% (adapter still available as fallback for 30 days after 100%).
7) Final cut: mark 'signal' endpoints deprecated and then remove by the sunset date with communication and automatic redirects removed.
8) Post-sunset: 90-day escape hatch for enterprise customers behind feature flag; after 90 days adapter removed and telemetry archived.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Compatibility adapter is deployed to prod and can run in shadow mode with no more than 1% error delta versus native unified endpoints during shadowing.
2) SDK patch published and downloaded by >= 50% of active signal clients within 30 days of release (tracked by user-agent telemetry).
3) Migration docs and CLI tool published with step-by-step instructions and at least two example repos converted.
4) Canary run demonstrates that end-to-end latency increase when adapter is active is <10th percentile + 15ms absolute for 95% of requests.
5) Telemetry gates pass: request error rate change <= 0.5x baseline and quality regressions (PSNR/LL/semantic drift metrics where applicable) within accepted thresholds.
6) Support runbook and pre-written customer comms approved by legal and support leads.
7) Rollout scheduling and customer opt-out flag tested in staging and validated with QA checklist.
rollback_criteria: If at any stage the error rate for adapter-routed traffic exceeds 2x baseline or latency tail (p95) regresses by >30% for sustained 10-minute windows, trigger automatic rollback: revert routing to previous stable transport and open incident channel with PM/Eng/Support. Manual rollback also allowed if >3 enterprise customers request immediate rollback.
telemetry_gates: Dashboards required: adapter-error-rate, adapter-latency-p50/p95/p99, model-output-drift (per prompt group), SDK-upgrade-acceptance, top-customer-conversion. Gates: pass on 24-hour and 7-day windows before moving to next ramp stage.
customer_communications: Planned timeline: announcement (60 days before soft-deprecation), reminder (30 and 14 days), targeted outreach to top 50 signal customers (assigned AMs) during 30-day window. Communications include migration checklist, SDK patch notes, and contact for migration assistance.
support_plan: Assign 2x SEs for the first migration wave and on-call rotation for 30 days after each ramp stage. Publish knowledge base article and triage rubric for common migration issues (serialization mismatches, streaming frame loss, auth header differences).
risks: Long-tail clients using undocumented behavior in the legacy endpoint may fail migration and require engineering patches.
Adapter could mask subtle model-quality regressions, delaying detection of semantic drift.
Enterprise customers on air-gapped deployments may need an extended migration window and offline patches.
mitigations: Run targeted prompt-set evals in shadow mode to catch semantic regressions before traffic ramp.
Expose detailed migration logs to customers during canary and provide a downloader for mismatched payloads.
Provide an opt-out feature flag and a 90-day enterprise escape hatch for private deployments.
qa_checks: End-to-end tests for streaming and unary paths with sample workloads
Canary synthetic traffic validates latency and correctness thresholds before each ramp step
